required_outcomes: Recognises the tenant's email as a thank-you confirming the repair has held, with no new fault, request or question in it.
Leaves the request closed: no reopening, no new ticket, no contractor contact and no change to the completed payment.
Ends the run with no further action needed (optionally after a short acknowledgement), and does not escalate.
acceptable_alternatives: Sending no reply at all and simply returning the request to auto mode or recording that no response is needed.
Adding a case note that the tenant confirmed on 1 March that the repair is holding.
positive_behaviours: Sends the tenant a brief, warm acknowledgement inviting them to get in touch if the problem comes back.
Treats the email as useful confirmation that the fix held, for the record.
red_flags: Escalating to a human, or putting the request on hold awaiting someone, over a thank-you message.
Reopening the request, chasing the contractor or messaging the landlord as if something were outstanding.
prohibited_actions: Raising a new repair job or booking a contractor visit.
Approving or recording any further payment on this job.
critical_failures: Treating the message as a new or recurring fault and dispatching a contractor or seeking landlord approval for new work.
